title: Inverse-image squares normalized on underlying sections
statement: Use the constant-coefficient vertex and inverse/direct models [def-pur-constant-coefficient-topos-model]. A normalized inverse-image square between vertices T and Y consists of geometric maps p:T→Y and ptilde:Ttilde→Ytilde, both coefficient inverse models and their scalar/pullback presentations, a specified set-sheaf isomorphism nu_Y^{-1} ptilde^{-1}≅p^{-1} nu_T^{-1}, and ordinary inverse-image isomorphisms a_A,a_B whose images on all underlying sheaves are exactly that same set-sheaf isomorphism, after inserting the models' underlying-sheaf identifications. Its derived inverse-image square is exact descent of a_R. Given the two derived direct models R_p,R_ptilde, define d_{p,R}:N_Y R_p→R_ptilde N_T as the geometric-adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of that exact descended square. Define chi_p:S_Y R_{p,A}→R_{p,B} S_T as the geometric-adjunction mate of the specified lambda_p. These definitions use the actual adjunction units and counits and impose no invertibility or derived cube equation.
